what: Kev-0.8B: int8 measured, not shipped. int8lin (every decoder linear int8 per block of 32) fails the bar; the fp32 torch bisect with the exporter's own int8 weights under a rule written before any result (bisect/rule.json) chose no set; int8mix (layers 0-11 fp16, outside the rule) passes. Exports, gates, red arms, the bisect table and the summary. Every int8 graph here is the unrolled S = 16 form (the first upload's graph); the fp32 Metal-kernel forms were not measured in int8. Process ids removed in round 17 (no number or result changed).

readout_int8lin.readout: one row per question, fresh zero states per row; a row of T ids runs as ceil(T / 16) calls of 'main' (static S = 16): call k gets ids[16k : 16k + 16] with position_ids 0..16k+15; the last call is padded with <|endoftext|> (248044) and the hidden rows of the padded positions are discarded (causal: they cannot reach a real position). The hidden rows [1, 16, 1024] of every call, concatenated and cut to T, are the backbone's final-norm last_hidden_state [T, 1024] the head reads. A row fits when ceil(T / 16) * 16 <= 4095 (the position dim's upper bound; the KV sequence dim is allocated at 4096).

rule.target: worst max|dp| over the 60 bisect rows < 0.010 (0.5 x the gate bar 0.02; every option of every question, near-ties included), this instrument
rule.reproduction_check: before any selection: all_int8's worst max|dp| over the bisect rows (this instrument) >= 0.5 x the int8lin gate transcript's worst over the same rows; otherwise stop and report (the gate's error would not be the int8 weights')
rule.instrument_floor: exact must reproduce the round-2 P1 run (parity/p1_shard*.jsonl) of every bisect row bit for bit (probabilities), and every process's swap-back re-run likewise
rule.size: a set's size = the params of the linears it keeps out of int8 (the bytes it costs)
rule.cap: a candidate keeps at most 50% of the body's linear params out of int8
search: 1. fixed configs: exact, all_int8, layer_NN_fp16 (24), gdn_fp16, attn_fp16, mlp_fp16, proj_<kind>_fp16 (12)

2. layer sets: the 24 layers ranked by their layer_NN_fp16 worst (ascending; ties: the lower index); L_k = the top k, for k = 2, 3, ... while within the cap; at the first k whose L_k meets the target (k = 1: the best single), also every k-subset of the top k+1 layers

3. kind sets: the 12 kinds ranked by their proj_<kind>_fp16 worst (ascending; ties: the order qkv z a b out q k v o gate up down); K_j = the top j, for j = 2, 3, ... while within the cap; at the first j whose K_j meets the target, also every j-subset of the top j+1 kinds; gdn_fp16 / attn_fp16 / mlp_fp16 are kind sets too

4. only if no set of steps 1-3 meets the target: unions L_k + K_j (k, j >= 1, the top-k / top-j sets of 2 and 3) within the cap, in ascending size (ties: smaller k, then smaller j), evaluated in that order until the first that meets the target, at most 12 of them
rule.choose: among the layer and kind sets of steps 1-3 that meet the target, the smallest size (ties: the layer set, then the lexicographically smallest sorted list); if none, the first union of step 4 that meets it; if none, no set (report the numbers: the ship form is the supervisor's call)
rule.then: the chosen set is exported (export_decoder.py int8mix) and gated on all 434 rows with the gate's own bar, then on the 130 held-out rows (never used to choose)

bisect_rule.why_rows: the top 30 rows of the int8lin gate by max|dp| (ties: oracle order), then 30 rows drawn from the other 404 rows by source (proportional, largest remainder, at least one per source; numpy default_rng(20261003).choice without replacement inside each source, sources in sorted order)
bisect_rule.estimate: 10,431 tokens per config; at round 2's 7.5 ms per token (1 thread, bmm conv) about 78 s per config
